strengths: Solid theoretical contributions: Star-shaped formulation is mathematically sound with correct VLB proof enabling compatibility with pre-trained models
Insightful connection to ReMDM that explains hyperparameter sensitivity and motivates proposed approach

Comprehensive experimental ablations validating design choices: two-phase generation analysis (Section 4.2), guided vs. unguided comparison (Section 4.3), and systematic hyperparameter studies (Appendix C)
Demonstrates practical improvements across multiple domains: text generation (OpenWebText), code generation (Conala), and instruction-tuned LLMs (Dream-Instruct 7B)
Parameter-efficient design: lightweight error predictor (single head training) adds negligible overhead while achieving significant gains in medium-step regimes
Strong reproducibility: code provided, detailed implementation details in appendices, uses public datasets/models, honest limitations discussion
Effective presentation with clear problem motivation, well-designed visualizations (Figures 1-3), and thorough appendix documentation
weaknesses: Limited novelty: Star-shaped formulation adapts continuous prior work (Okhotin et al. 2023), error prediction is straightforward binary classification; contribution is primarily empirical validation of combined approach

Fundamental limitation of star-shaped approach: pure star-shaped sampling fails, requiring hybrid MDLM+Star design for only final 20-40% of generation, suggesting core method has significant limitations
Incomplete baseline comparisons: missing empirical comparisons with GIDD, informed correctors, and other recent discrete diffusion guidance methods despite citing them
Modest absolute improvements: Dream-Instruct gains are 1-3 points on benchmarks; OpenWebText improvements come with diversity loss (DIV: 44.7→35.3 at 128 steps), complicating interpretation
Insufficient error predictor analysis: no metrics on detection accuracy, false positive rates, or sensitivity to model changes; single Figure 7 example for qualitative validation

Quality-diversity tradeoff not fully resolved: refinement helps perplexity but hurts diversity, MAUVE actually declines at 512 steps (Table 1: 58.6→56.3 with more refinement), suggesting optimization challenges
Missing computational cost analysis: no inference time comparison, refinement loops add steps but overhead not quantified; no analysis of computational fairness vs. ReMDM

Limited experimental scope: modest model scale (Dream-Instruct 7B), no human evaluation, no failure case analysis, max sequence length only 1280 tokens, no comparison with continuous latent diffusion approaches
Hyperparameter sensitivity remains: despite ReMDM improvements, τ_remask still requires tuning (Figure 6 shows optimal range T≈4-32); 10% loop size is heuristic-based
Fundamental limitations reduce applicability: no insertion/deletion operations, requires separate error predictor training for each model, cannot extend to variable-length generation

strengths: Sound theoretical framework with formal proof of VLB simplification (Claim 1) and elegant connection to ReMDM (Proposition 1), enabling reuse of pre-trained weights without fine-tuning

Compelling two-phase generation insight (Section 4.2): systematic analysis identifying that star-shaped sampling should only apply in late stages (~30% of steps) while preserving stability of early context-building phase
Principled error predictor design trained on actual diffusion errors rather than synthetic noise, addressing key limitation of confidence-based methods relying on miscalibrated confidence scores

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple domains (OWT, Conala, instruction-tuned 7B) with principled Pareto frontier analysis, extensive ablations on loop size/temperature/capacity, and strong out-of-domain robustness (AUC-ROC ≥0.84)

Consistent improvements across 7 diverse benchmarks (Table 1: +1.3 to +2.9 points) and superior performance in medium-step regimes (64-256 steps), with clear advantages at 128 steps over full-budget baselines
Excellent presentation with clear algorithms, comprehensive appendices, practical guidance for hyperparameter tuning, and informative visualizations (especially Appendix F remasking pattern analysis)
weaknesses: Limited novelty relative to ReMDM: method is mathematically equivalent to ReMDM with σ_t = 1 - α_{t-1}, with core novelty being learned guidance instead of heuristic scheduling; concurrent work (Kim et al., 2025; Huang et al., 2025) explores similar directions but receives limited discussion

Modest improvements in high-step regimes: at 512 steps, improvements narrow significantly; on Conala code generation (Table 2), gains over ReMDM are incremental; gains of ~1-3 MMLU points are useful but not dramatic

Significant practical overhead: 50% latency increase for 12B,H variant (3.43s vs 2.26s); 192 vs 128 NFEs for better-quality models; requires task-specific error predictor training (different datasets for different models), limiting claimed 'universality'

Theoretical gaps in early-stage coherence loss: Section 4.2 provides intuition but lacks formal analysis of why x_t independence causes degradation; distributional alignment between training (ground truth x₀ available) and inference (errors unknown) not rigorously justified

Acknowledged limitations reduce applicability: cannot perform insertion/deletion (only in-place substitution); requires separate sequential error predictor training; no aggressive throughput optimization; these meaningfully constrain real-world deployment

Experimental and methodological concerns: out-of-domain evaluation uses only text domains (no code→math or more distant shifts); hyperparameter sensitivity acknowledged but remains high (multiple temperatures and scheduling parameters); Pareto frontier in Figure 4 is busy and difficult to parse
